note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure.
  - Widespread itchy, sore, red skin consistent with eczema flare; worst on inner elbows; also chest, hands, and arms. Dry skin with cracked areas. No weeping reported.
  - No specific trigger identified; no change in emollients or shower product.
- Symptom timeline and progression.
  - Past few days; getting worse over the last few days.
- ENT symptoms (as applicable): throat swelling/closure sensation, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea, distribution of swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face), ear/neck symptoms.
  - Breathing reported as OK.
  - No other ENT airway or facial/oral swelling symptoms reported in transcript.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments (including any prior hospital care or injection therapy).
  - History of eczema; previously used over-the-counter hydrocortisone; previously tried an over-the-counter antihistamine (cetirizine) without improvement.
  - No prior ED visits or injection therapy mentioned.
- Allergies and current medications (mark missing dose/route/frequency as not documented).
  - Allergies: No known drug allergies.
  - Current/ongoing: Diprobase emollient; “Dermal” shower product; over-the-counter hydrocortisone (not helping; dose/route/frequency not documented); “blue” reliever inhaler for asthma used as needed (name/dose/route/frequency not documented); not currently taking antihistamines.
- Any relevant social context (e.g., accompaniment/supervision).
  - Not stated.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution (e.g., lips, tongue, uvula, face) if stated.
  - Not recorded.
- Airway/breathing descriptors if stated (e.g., stridor, work of breathing).
  - Patient reports breathing OK; no acute respiratory distress described.
- Mental status and associated features (e.g., dizziness, syncope) if stated.
  - Not recorded.
- Vitals and examination findings only if mentioned; otherwise note “Not recorded.”
  - Not recorded.
- Presence of another person with the patient (if stated).
  - Not recorded.

Assessment:
- Worsening widespread eczema flare with pruritus and xerosis/fissuring; no ENT airway involvement reported.
  - Justification: Rapid worsening over days; distribution (chest, hands/arms, inner elbows); dry/cracked skin; no weeping; breathing OK.
- Asthma, stable by history; intermittent use of “blue” inhaler.
- No known drug allergies.
- Conflict noted: family history stated as mother with hypothyroidism; clinician repeated “hyperthyroidism.”

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Prescribed fexofenadine (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Prescribed topical Betnovate: apply small amount (fingertip unit guidance provided) twice daily for the next 2 weeks.
  - Continue emollients: Dermal shower product and Diprobase (clinician later said “diprovate” — conflict noted).
  - Prescription sent to patient’s nominated pharmacy (Boots) for collection.
- Specific instructions provided to patient/caregiver:
  - Continue current emollients alongside new treatments.
  - Use Betnovate twice daily for 2 weeks in thin layers as instructed.
  - “If there’s no improvement, you need to get back to us.”
  - If any adverse or allergic reaction occurs, “get in touch with us.”
  - “If things are getting worse in the next two weeks, call us before hand.”
- Escalation criteria/red flags:
  - Contact the service if symptoms worsen or if any adverse/allergic reaction occurs (as above).
- Follow-up:
  - Self-monitor; contact service earlier if worsening or no improvement; otherwise re-evaluate after 2 weeks as advised.
  - No ENT/allergy referral discussed.
- COVID-19 vaccine suitability:
  - Not discussed.

Quality checks:
- Missing clinically expected elements for acute ENT/allergy presentation:
  - Detailed ENT airway symptom review (throat tightness, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling) not performed/documented.
  - Objective exam of oropharynx/neck and respiratory effort not documented.
  - Vitals not recorded.
  - Fexofenadine dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - “Blue” inhaler medication name/dose/frequency not documented.
  - No discussion of potential triggers or avoidance measures beyond current products.
  - No emergency plan beyond “get in touch” if worsening/adverse reaction; no guidance on urgent/EMS activation.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Family history: mother reported to have hypothyroidism; clinician restated as hyperthyroidism (conflict noted).
  - Emollient product name: patient uses Diprobase; clinician later said “diprovate” (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality:
  - Some unclear/overlapping speech and incomplete phrases; medication names partially unclear. Overall sufficient to determine main assessment and plan.
